characters.name: 可可蝠
characters.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. EDIT the attached approved Batwalk portrait into a UNIVERSAL ANIMATION SPRITE SHEET. The supplied portrait is the exact character model, not a loose style reference. Preserve its exact individual face, silhouette construction, body/ear proportions, colors, original accessories and pixel rendering. Do not redesign, smooth, squash or stretch the character.
Invariants for 可可蝠: Tall chocolate-brown wrapped-wing cocoon; huge thick caramel furry shawl collar framing small friendly brown face, short pink-lined ears, pug nose with two tiny lip wattles, blushing cheeks, tiny feet. Preserve the tall blanket body and fluffy collar, never a round generic bat.
Flight: unfold the same long chocolate cloak-wings from the shoulders, retaining the thick tan collar and tall small body. Never turn into a round generic bat.
Output transparent PNG, 4 columns × 5 rows of SQUARE equally spaced cells, 20 poses total, portrait aspect ratio 4:5 (ideally 2048×2560). Each row has four consecutive animation keyframes of ONE action. Use the same character scale, camera distance and centered body registration in every cell. Choose a scale small enough for open flying wings and tallest ears; then KEEP it across all five rows. Leave at least 12% empty transparent margin INSIDE EACH CELL. Nothing may touch cell borders or overlap neighboring cells. No grid lines, text, labels, letters, scenery, shadows, props except the tiny edible fruit, or other characters. Same Gentle pixel: clean stepped dark outlines, warm gentle colors, soft pixel-cluster shading, hard-edged pixels and actual alpha transparency.
ROW 1 IDLE: frame1 faithfully match the original resting portrait; frame2 a small attentive ear/eye glance; frame3 a soft blink and a little original wing-tip settling; frame4 settle back towards the original pose. Body proportions stay unchanged. A quiet loop, no jumping.
ROW 2 SLEEP: ALL FOUR frames show visibly closed sleepy eyes, with the same original wings gently wrapped/relaxed. frame1 calm sleep; frame2 tiny ear twitch; frame3 slightly lift then settle a wing tip while sleeping; frame4 relaxed sleep again. Do not use Z letters, pillows, hats not already in the reference, perches or branches. No full-body squashing/breathing deformation.
ROW 3 FLY: four clear phases of a wing beat using the TWO EXISTING wings: wings raised, extended out, lowered, extended again. Body remains centered at the SAME size, only a subtle lift. Keep original body, face, ears and accessories; do not replace its wings with a generic template or invent extra limbs. Whole wings fully fit within every cell.
ROW 4 PET: no human hand. frame1 original pose noticing a pat; frame2 leans head slightly into affection with happy closed eyes; frame3 existing wing tips/ears relax with one TINY peach heart beside head; frame4 contented original pose. Keep whole-body shape stable, no body stretch.
ROW 5 EAT: frame1 holds a tiny piece of fruit with its original wing/thumb at mouth; frame2 takes a bite; frame3 chews with pleased closed eyes; frame4 satisfied after swallowing. Use the reference fruit if present; otherwise a tiny red berry. Do not add arms/hands, change belly or enlarge cheeks. Fruit never covers the face.
Exactly two original wings and two original feet. Distinct motion in each row with a calm beginning/end. The neutral frame should feel like the original portrait simply came to life. Absolutely no new character design.
